solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Post spy outside English royal house (11)

indicators.note: the spy's letters sit outside E, wrapping it

blocks.note: to post someone somewhere is to plant them there

annotation.surface: An espionage plot: a spy is stationed just outside the palace of an English royal family.
annotation.walkthrough: "Post spy" reads as one order to station a spy, but each word is its own piece, and "English" is the letter hidden inside the second.
annotation.definitionFit: The Plantagenets were the royal house that ruled England from Henry II to Richard III.

clue.text: Time to abandon bet? That’s a joke (3)

indicators.note: T abandons the word for bet, so it is taken out

blocks.note: a punt is a bet (British slang)

annotation.surface: Someone told it is time to give up gambling replies that the idea is laughable.
annotation.walkthrough: A punt is British slang for a wager; drop its T and the joke is left.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun is a joke built on a word's double sense or sound.

clue.text: Trouble in the past overwhelming centre of Zagreb (5)

indicators.note: AGO covers and swallows the middle letters
take the middle letters of Zagreb

blocks.note: the two middle letters of ZaGReb

annotation.surface: A historical note about unrest that once engulfed the Croatian capital.
annotation.walkthrough: Zagreb has six letters, so its centre is a pair, GR, not a single letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for aggressive trouble or hassle.

clue.text: Birds ultimately flaunt it over rodents (7)

indicators.note: take the last letter of flaunt
in a down clue, the first pieces sit over the rodents

annotation.surface: Birds finally show off in front of the mice below them.
annotation.walkthrough: "it" is taken literally, and the birds show off by sitting over the mice in the column.
annotation.definitionFit: Titmice, or tits, are small songbirds.

clue.text: Good to get involved again: it should bear fruit (9)

blocks.note: to re-engage is to get involved again

annotation.surface: A pep talk: getting back into things is good and will pay off.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bear fruit" pretends to mean succeed, echoing the pep-talk surface, but a greengage tree literally bears fruit.
annotation.definitionFit: A greengage is a plum tree, which bears the green plums of the same name.

clue.text: Scandinavian goddesses, and not Poles (5)

blocks.note: the North and South poles, N and S

annotation.surface: A clarification that these northern goddesses are not from Poland.
annotation.walkthrough: "Poles" wants to be the people of Poland; here it is the two magnetic poles, N and S.
annotation.definitionFit: The Norns are the three goddesses of fate in Norse mythology.

clue.text: Support premier accepting Republican crown (7)

indicators.note: the pieces take R in, after their first letter

blocks.note: a golf tee supports the ball

annotation.surface: Politics: backing a prime minister who has taken the Republican crown.
annotation.walkthrough: "Crown" is set up as a political prize, but it is the crown of a tree.
annotation.definitionFit: Botanists call the leafy upper part of a tree its crown, the part a royal crown sits on for a person.

clue.text: Nip backwards and forwards serving fizzy drink (3)

indicators.note: the word reads the same either way

blocks.note: to nip is to make a quick trip, into a shop or out for a moment

annotation.surface: A barman darting to and fro handing out fizzy drinks.
annotation.walkthrough: To nip into a shop is to pop into it, and POP reads the same both ways.
annotation.definitionFit: Named for the sound the cork or cap makes, pop is the informal word for a carbonated soft drink.

clue.text: So a plant’s unexpectedly situated behind a hooter (9)

indicators.note: the letters turn up in an unexpected order

annotation.surface: Someone surprised to find a plant placed behind a car horn.
annotation.walkthrough: A hooter is British slang for a nose, not the car horn the surface suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: Postnasal means situated behind the nose, as in postnasal drip.

clue.text: Spreader of alarm, one who sells grass? (11)

annotation.surface: An alarmist is likened to someone dealing cannabis.
annotation.walkthrough: Panic is a genus of grass (panic grass), so a seller of it would be a panic-monger; the question mark flags the whimsy.
annotation.definitionFit: A panicmonger stirs up alarm, spreading panic.

clue.text: Tailored thing you and I regularly assume at first when retiring (9)

definitions.text: Tailored thing you and I regularly assume at first when retiring

indicators.note: THING is cut and restyled into new order
take the first letters of regularly and assume
those two letters go backwards

annotation.surface: A description of pyjamas: the fitted garment we routinely put on when going to bed.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: nightwear is what you and I regularly put on when retiring to bed. "Retiring" does double duty as bedtime and reversal.
annotation.definitionFit: Nightwear is clothing worn in bed, which is exactly what we assume on retiring.

clue.text: Headland backing on east German city (5)

indicators.note: the headland word reads backwards
in an across clue, it comes after E

blocks.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's shores or Orford Ness

annotation.surface: A coastal promontory lying behind the east side of a German city.
annotation.walkthrough: Ness is an old word for a headland, common in British place names.
annotation.definitionFit: Essen is a large city in Germany's Ruhr.

clue.text: Ideal article on posh tropical headgear (7)

indicators.note: in an across clue, the article comes after the posh headgear

blocks.note: a topi is a sun helmet

annotation.surface: A remark that a fancy tropical hat is the perfect accessory.
annotation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is a crossword staple; a topi is the pith helmet of the colonial tropics.
annotation.definitionFit: Utopian means ideal, like the perfect society of More's Utopia.

clue.text: Subscriber runs in without a plan? (11)

indicators.note: R goes in the word for without a plan

annotation.surface: A magazine subscriber who signs up on impulse.
annotation.walkthrough: "Subscriber" means one who signs underneath, not one who buys a magazine.
annotation.definitionFit: The undersigned is the person who has signed, literally subscribed, the document.

clue.text: Diabolical cast in a play (7)

indicators.note: the letters are played with, moved around

annotation.surface: A reviewer panning the dreadful cast of a stage play.
annotation.walkthrough: "Diabolical" sounds like a critic's verdict on the actors, but it is the literal devilish meaning.
annotation.definitionFit: Satanic means of or like Satan, hence diabolical.

clue.text: Buccaneer finally turned libertine (5)

indicators.note: take the last letter of turned

blocks.note: a rake is a dissolute man

annotation.surface: A pirate who eventually became a debauchee.
annotation.walkthrough: Sir Francis Drake was an Elizabethan privateer, which the Spanish counted as a pirate.
annotation.definitionFit: Drake raided Spanish ships and ports, a buccaneer in all but commission.

clue.text: A modification accepted by both sides in Russian port (9)

indicators.note: the modification is taken in between the two sides

blocks.note: right and left, R and L

annotation.surface: An amendment that both parties agree to in a Russian harbour negotiation.
annotation.walkthrough: "Both sides" sounds like two negotiating parties but gives R and L, right and left.
annotation.definitionFit: Archangel (Arkhangelsk) is a port on the White Sea in northern Russia.

clue.text: A new piece of advice regarding hors d’oeuvre (9)

blocks.note: a tip is a piece of advice

annotation.surface: A fresh suggestion about what to serve as a starter.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as menu advice, which is exactly where the answer belongs.
annotation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian hors d'oeuvre served before the pasta.

clue.text: Soak up air circulating in strange animal enclosure (9)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the soak word reads upwards
the letters of air move round
the stirred air sits inside strange

blocks.note: to ret flax is to soak it

annotation.surface: Absorbing the air that swirls around an odd zoo enclosure.
annotation.walkthrough: "Soak up" is not absorb: it is RET turned upwards. Rum is British for odd.
annotation.definitionFit: A terrarium is a glass enclosure for keeping small land animals or plants.

clue.text: Wide boy in poem always after tennis equipment (9)

indicators.note: the poetic always comes after the tennis equipment

blocks.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

annotation.surface: A spiv in a poem forever chasing tennis kit.
annotation.walkthrough: A wide boy is British slang for a small-time crook or spiv.
annotation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs dishonest schemes, as a wide boy does.

clue.text: European king in ceremony connected to American state (7)

indicators.note: the king goes inside the ceremony
to be connected to something is to be joined on to it, so A is joined to the end of what precedes it

annotation.surface: A European monarch at a ceremony linked to one of the United States.
annotation.walkthrough: "American state" wants to be read together as one of the fifty; A is American and "state" alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Eritrea is an independent state in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Silence about limits of unusual prison (5)

indicators.note: GAG goes around the letters
take the outer letters of unusual

blocks.note: first and last letters of UnusuaL

annotation.surface: Hushing up the extent of an unusual jail.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface fits the answer: the gulag was where dissidents were silenced.
annotation.definitionFit: The Gulag was the Soviet system of forced-labour prison camps.

clue.text: Sailing ship in strong wind about to cross lake (7)

indicators.note: the wind and about pieces lie across L, holding it

blocks.note: a gale is a strong wind

annotation.surface: A sailing ship in a gale, about to cross a lake.
annotation.walkthrough: "About to cross" reads as on the point of crossing; ON is about, and GALE takes in L.
annotation.definitionFit: A galleon is a large square-rigged sailing ship.

clue.text: Child in game extremely curious about boxer’s slanting script (7)

indicators.note: take the extreme letters of curious
the curious letters are placed about, that is next to, the boxer, after him

blocks.note: the child who chases the others in tag is 'it'
first and last letters of CuriouS

annotation.surface: A curious child in a game studying a boxer's slanted handwriting.
annotation.walkthrough: "Boxer's" is possessive in the surface but just gives ALI; the 's belongs to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The sloping typeface is named for Italy, where it was first cut in the 1500s to imitate slanted handwriting.

clue.text: Direct course of ox, perhaps (5)

blocks.note: a verb: guide the path of a vehicle or ship
a noun: a young castrated bull, 'perhaps' because an ox is only one example

annotation.surface: Guiding the path of an ox.
annotation.walkthrough: Both senses sit naturally together, which hides the join between them: you might well steer a steer.
annotation.definitionFit: One word covers a helmsman's verb and a cattle farmer's noun, the young bullock raised for beef.

clue.text: Key singers upset following lines using celebs only (3-4)

indicators.note: the singers are turned over, reading backwards
the reversed singers come after the lines

blocks.note: to sing is to inform; informers are rats

annotation.surface: Chorus members upset that the show's lines were given only to celebrities.
annotation.walkthrough: Singers here are informers (one who sings to the police), so RATS, which turns into STAR.
annotation.definitionFit: An all-star production uses only famous performers.

clue.text: Encountered going north, work up speed (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, MET reads upwards
in a down clue, 'up' means read from the bottom, so OP climbs to PO

annotation.surface: Meeting someone heading north who urges you to work faster.
annotation.walkthrough: "Work up speed" looks like a phrase meaning accelerate, but it splits into wordplay and definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Tempo is speed, especially the pace of music.

clue.text: African country reflecting about mother’s ruin (5)

indicators.note: as in a mirror, the letters read backwards

blocks.note: mother's ruin is British slang for gin

annotation.surface: A country pondering the disgrace of someone's mother.
annotation.walkthrough: Mother's ruin is an old British nickname for gin.
annotation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked country in West Africa.

clue.text: Like protective layer originally required to stop widespread disease (9)

indicators.note: take the first letter of required
R plugs the middle of the disease word

blocks.note: an epidemic is a widespread disease

annotation.surface: A protective coating is needed to halt an outbreak.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a public-health message about masks or barriers; the protective layer is the skin.
annotation.definitionFit: Epidermic means relating to the epidermis, the skin's protective outer layer.

clue.text: Healthy food: price reduced by 25 per cent (3)

indicators.note: a four-letter word loses one letter, a quarter of it

annotation.surface: A supermarket promotion: healthy food at a quarter off.
annotation.walkthrough: Cos is a lettuce, romaine to Americans.
annotation.definitionFit: A lettuce is the definition by example: named for the Greek island of Kos, it is a crisp salad leaf, virtuous eating.

clue.text: Pulse ideally occurring at periodic intervals (3)

indicators.note: letters that occur at regular intervals are every second one, so take alternate letters

annotation.surface: A heartbeat that ideally comes at regular intervals.
annotation.walkthrough: "Pulse" suggests a heartbeat, matching the regular-interval surface; it is the lentil kind.
annotation.definitionFit: Dal is split lentils or other pulses, and the dish made from them.

clue.text: Acerbic representation of Maori cousin (11)

indicators.note: the letters are re-presented in a new order

annotation.surface: A sharp-tongued portrayal of a New Zealand relative.
annotation.walkthrough: A clean anagram; the surface is a family portrait with bite.
annotation.definitionFit: Acrimonious means bitter and sharp, as acerbic does.
